name: Café Hafa
hero_subtitle: Terraces stacked above the strait — Tangier’s most famous café pause.

overview.title: Mint Tea on the Cliff
overview.p1: Café Hafa is less about the coffee than about the seat. Terraces step down the cliff, mint tea arrives in glasses, and the Strait of Gibraltar does the rest. Writers and musicians made it famous; locals still use it as a place to sit and watch the light change.
overview.p2: You do not need a long stay. An hour with a tea is enough. Come for late afternoon if you want the softer colours; mornings are quieter if you dislike crowds.
overview.p3: It is a café with a view, not a full restaurant experience — keep expectations there and you will leave happy.

q1.question: Do I need a reservation?
q1.answer: Usually not for tea; weekends and sunset can fill the best tiers.

q2.question: Is food served?
q2.answer: Light options may be available — tea and the view are the main event.

q3.question: How do I get there?
q3.answer: Taxi or a walk from the medina side; ask your riad for the current easiest approach.

q4.question: Do I need a guide at Café Hafa?
q4.answer: Optional for a simple visit; useful for historical context.

q5.question: Is Café Hafa suitable for families?
q5.answer: Yes with normal supervision on steps, cliffs or wet stone.

food.title: Tea first
food.p1: Mint tea is the classic order. Eat a proper meal elsewhere if you are hungry.
food.p2: You are paying for time and a view as much as for the tea.
food.li2: Second glass if you settle in
food.li3: Snack only if offered and fresh
food.li4: Dinner later in the medina or ville nouvelle
food.li5: Water if the day is hot
